pipeline_name: Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America System

validity.recommendation: Leave Diameter blank as recorded -- the Texas-Louisiana Expansion Project (FERC Docket CP24-8-000) is a compressor-station-only project on Natural's existing Louisiana Line; do not carry the wiki's system-level '24 inches' onto it.
validity.researcher_notes: Checked whether this project (Kinder Morgan subsidiary Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America LLC, 'Natural,' proposed status, StartYear1 2026) lays new pipe before treating the blank Diameter as owed a fill (compression-only-expansion rule). FERC's order issuing the certificate, 189 FERC P 61,131, Docket No. CP24-8-000, issued 2024-11-21 (read in full via pdftotext from a university-hosted mirror of the filed order, aglaw.psu.edu) states the ENTIRE proposal: modify existing Compressor Station 302 (Montgomery County, TX) by installing one new 18,340 HP electric-motor-driven compressor unit, uprating two existing EMD units by 1,600 HP each, and re-wheeling all three; modify existing Compressor Station 343 (Liberty County, TX) by re-wheeling two existing EMD units; and install auxiliary facilities (gas cooling equipment, motor control center buildings, filter separators, station yard piping) at both stations. No new mainline pipe or loop is proposed. The order separately states Natural's existing 'Louisiana Line is composed of two 30-inch-diameter pipelines' running from Compressor Station 302 east to Vermilion Parish, LA -- i.e. the pipe this project adds capacity ON TO is 30-inch, not the wiki's 24-inch figure, which is presumably a different segment/lateral of the wider NGPL System infobox rather than this specific project. Capacity matches the sheet closely: the order authorizes 300,000 Dth/d of new eastbound firm transportation on Segment 25 of the Louisiana Line (sheet Capacity = 300000.00 Dth/d, CapacityUnits 'Dth/d' -- exact match), part of a total 467,000 Dth/d project. Independent corroboration (trade press, Pipeline & Gas Journal, pgjonline.com): '$72 million' project, 'Compressor Station 302... increase the total certificated horsepower... from 26,800 to 48,340,' confirms compressor-only scope and the $72M cost. A second independent corroboration: FERC's own Notice of Availability of the Environmental Assessment (federalregister.gov, 2024-06-12) for the same docket/project name. Three independent origins (FERC order text, pgjonline.com, federalregister.gov) agree this is compression/auxiliary-facility work on an EXISTING 30-inch line, not new pipe -- so the blank Diameter is correct and this flag resolves as a confirmation, not a fill, per the compression-only-expansion rule.
